category_title: Struggling readers who view reading as a process of remembering and repeating
minimal_context: Alyssa is participating in a whole-class literacy activity where students are changing letters on a magnet board to make different words in the /an/ family.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Class, let's look at the magnet board. We are going to change the first letter to make different words in the /an/ family.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Attentively watches the teacher during the group instruction but does not focus on the print on the board.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's read this first word together. The word is 'pan'.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Sits quietly, silently mouthing the word as it is read by others, continuing to watch the teacher instead of looking at the board.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Now I am changing the first letter. Alyssa, what should we do to figure out how to read this?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: To do it over and over again, 'Cause if you do it over and over again, you’ll know how to read.

STUDENT: To do it over and over again, 'Cause if you do it over and over again, you’ll know how to read.
